answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so spawning many fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. The bond is a signal of commitment: honest agents keep their stake and build reputation over repeated rounds, while a summit of trusted attestors reviews behavior and releases rewards only to identities with consistent history. Like bees at one nectar source, sustained useful work, not sheer account count, earns standing, so splitting one bond across clones leaves each below the payment threshold.
